title: The effect of dnaA self-autoregulation: a molecular thermostat for the DnaA pool
caption: Three views of the dnaa-4 feedback making the DnaA pool self-stabilizing. (A) Homeostasis plateau: steady-state DnaA setpoint vs constitutive expression rate V (1.0/1.5/2.0e-3). With feedback OFF (control) the pool tracks V and runs out of band (490->895->1141); with feedback ON it is held flat in-band (295->333->343) - the feedback cancels the expression rate. (B) Phase portrait (promoter occupancy f -> DnaA pool): the autoregulated system settles on a tight attractor (blue density, setpoint ~330), while the same-V control drifts up and out (red). (C) The brake in real time (gens 5-9, V=1.5e-3): the control pool (red) sawtooths up out of the band while the dnaa-4 pool (blue) is held; the smoothed repression factor R = 1 - s*f^n/(K^n+f^n) (purple) drops as occupancy rises, cutting dnaA synthesis and pulling the pool back. s=0.7, K=0.5, n=4.
interpretation: Autoregulation converts the DnaA pool from an open-loop quantity set by the expression rate into a closed-loop homeostatic setpoint set by the feedback strength. The setpoint is ~330 molecules regardless of a 2x change in V; without feedback the same V change nearly triples the pool. This is the central dnaa-4 finding rendered mechanistically.
